title: Discriminative phonation in macaques: effects of anterior mesial cortex damage.
abstract: Lesion damage of the anterior midline hemisphere in M. mulatta results in impaired discriminative vocal activity. Destruction of the supplementary motor area (SMA) or pre-SMA greatly increases vocal response latency without similar changes in a non-vocal response. Discrimination and efficiency in performing the vocal and non-vocal responses are unaffected by this damage. The behavioral deficit reflects a specific loss in initiating vocal signals.
